items.prompt: Orthographic top-down architectural plan photograph of a real built film set, taken straight down from high above: camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground; no wall face, no elevation, no side of any building, wall, hedge or tree trunk is visible; only the ground plane, the top edges of walls and hedges and the tops of trees, furniture and objects are seen. The top of the image is north. Plan of a 48 by 27 metre stretch of an 1860s English shingle beach in an Art Nouveau dream after Alphonse Mucha, built as a real location set. The left quarter of the image is calm pale jade-grey sea with small curling wavelets. The waterline runs from top to bottom about 30 percent from the left, in a gentle flowing curve. From the waterline to about 62 percent across lies a broad strip of firm, flat, wet sand, smooth and reflective; along its right edge a curving line of white dried foam and shell grit marks the tide-line. From there to the right edge rises a bank of rounded grey and fawn flint shingle, with sea-kale tufts near the right edge. On the upper beach, about 70 percent across and exactly at mid-height, a low flat-topped grey rock ledge about 3 metres long and 1.5 metres deep sits alone on the shingle, its top seen from above with curving flowing strata, draped bladderwrack and sea-pinks in its cracks, a small rock pool beside it. Near the top of the image a dark weathered timber groyne runs from the shingle across the sand into the sea, its posts capped with verdigris iron wave-scroll finials. On the wet sand below-left of centre two small wooden spades stand upright, nobody near them. On the shingle below-right of the ledge a few stranded lobster pots and a coil of old rope. Low golden evening sun from the west (over the sea, left) with long shadows toward the east, sparkle on the water. The set is empty: no people, no animals, no creatures, no text, no labels, no arrows, no symbols, no map legend. A clean, sharp, evenly exposed photographic plan in which every feature named above is clearly readable in its stated position. Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
